title: Media Testing, Batch Qualification, and Reuse Decisions
objective: Build a controlled media-qualification program that connects sampling, physical and chemical tests, crop trials, contamination risk, and release decisions.

terms.definition: Documented evaluation determining whether a media lot is fit for intended use.
Composite or selected sample designed to reflect the material or crop zone being evaluated.
Method collecting displaced pore solution from an irrigated container for pH/EC testing.
Documented response that corrects a problem and reduces recurrence.

coreScience: Media qualification begins before planting. Confirm supplier, formulation, lot, packaging integrity, storage, moisture, odor, pests, foreign material, and label claims. Then test properties tied to the intended system: pH, EC, air space, container capacity, bulk density, particle distribution, nutrients, sodium/chloride, maturity, or pathogens as applicable.

Extraction methods are not interchangeable. Pour-through, saturated media extract, and 1:2 dilution use different sample preparation and produce different numerical ranges. Trend comparisons require the same method, meter calibration, timing, moisture state, container, and sampling location.

Reuse is a risk decision, not an automatic sustainability win. Residual roots, salts, unbalanced nutrients, decomposed particles, pests, pathogens, pesticide residues, and changed wettability must be weighed against cost, waste, treatment feasibility, legal limits, and crop value. Mixing unqualified used media into a new lot hides the history rather than removing it.

cultivationRelevance: Set written release, hold, recondition, downgrade, and reject criteria before results arrive. A small biological crop trial can reveal issues that chemical tests miss.
If reuse is allowed, assign a new batch ID and document source crop, sanitation or treatment, amendments, retesting, and destination. Never send suspect disease media into clean propagation.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Supplier, formula, lot, receipt, storage, sampler, date, and destination.
Plan, number of increments, locations, composite method, container, and preservation.
Method-specific pH/EC, physical properties, nutrients, contaminants, maturity, and pathogens.
Specification, result, release/hold/reject status, reviewer, and rationale.
Source history, treatment, amendment, retest, restricted use, follow-up, and prevention.

misconceptions: One runoff reading qualifies a media lot: It samples one container under one method and moisture history.
A sanitized container makes used media clean: The medium retains biological, chemical, and physical history.
Different pH/EC extraction methods should match: They create different dilutions and accepted interpretation ranges.
evidenceLimits: Specifications must be tailored to crop, container, irrigation, laboratory method, and jurisdiction. This volume does not establish universal cannabis pass/fail numbers.
